subject.title: Surface internal system messages in a distinct UI block instead of normal chat bubbles

question: Should visible runtime/system-originated messages be a dedicated user-facing diagnostic lane, hidden agent-only input, or both depending on explicit audience metadata?
rationale: The remaining work is not just CSS: it decides which internal messages belong in user-visible chat, what provenance travels through gateway projections, and how Control UI/WebChat should explain runtime-originated content.

options.title: Audience metadata plus diagnostic lane
options.body: Add explicit audience/provenance handling so agent-only runtime inputs stay hidden while intentionally visible system notices render in a labeled diagnostic block.

options.title: Presentation-only system styling
options.body: Keep current visibility rules and only add a distinct Control UI/WebChat system block for rows already projected as system messages.

options.title: Hide internal/system rows from chat
options.body: Route internal/system rows to logs or developer surfaces only, trading transparency for the cleanest end-user transcript.

recommendation.title: Audience metadata plus diagnostic lane
recommendation.body: Add explicit audience/provenance handling so agent-only runtime inputs stay hidden while intentionally visible system notices render in a labeled diagnostic block.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent display-projection and system-event work makes this the best available owner for deciding the user-visible runtime-message boundary.
